output.title: Solid-Fuel Atmosphere Coverage Flight Campaign
output.objective: Establish test evidence at the lunar exploration atmosphere and extend atmosphere coverage through fixed stepping-stone tests, building on published Saffire runs [saffire-iv-vi]. Under the dashboard’s atmosphere-distance rule, completing the plan would change the lunar target from Near tested to Tested; the staged-decompression Mars-transit target remains Tested, supported by nearby evidence including [saffire-v-2]. These labels describe atmosphere coverage, not demonstrated mission safety or gravity equivalence.

tests.purpose: Test 34% O2 at 8.2 psi total pressure, with 2.79 psi O2 partial pressure, directly at the lunar target, extending [saffire-vi-2], [saffire-vi-3] and [saffire-vi-4] from [saffire-iv-vi]. The point would establish behavior at the target atmosphere; [saffire-vi-4] supplies similar-pressure precedent at 8.01 psi, but every run in the data is microgravity, so this test needs a partial-gravity platform or a stated reason for flying in microgravity.
tests.measure: Record ignition yes/no, flame spread rate where applicable, and extinction or sustained burning, together with actual oxygen concentration, pressure, airflow and specimen configuration.

tests.purpose: Test 24% O2 at 7 psi total pressure, with 1.68 psi O2 partial pressure, stepping from [saffire-vi-4] with supporting comparisons to [saffire-vi-3] and [saffire-vi-2] in [saffire-iv-vi], to bring 8 untested grid squares within reach of evidence. This would extend lower-pressure atmosphere coverage; [cfi-1236] in [cfi] provides only similar-pressure precedent at 7.35 psi, not solid-fuel or oxygen-capability validation.
tests.measure: Record ignition yes/no, flame spread rate where applicable, and extinction or sustained burning, with actual atmosphere, airflow and specimen configuration.

tests.purpose: Test 29% O2 at 12 psi total pressure, with 3.48 psi O2 partial pressure, stepping from [saffire-v-4] and comparing with [saffire-v-2] and [saffire-v-3] in [saffire-iv-vi]. This would extend evidence toward higher pressure and bring 8 untested grid squares within reach; the supplied plan lists no similar-pressure hardware precedent for this point.
tests.measure: Record ignition yes/no, flame spread rate where applicable, and extinction or sustained burning, with actual atmosphere, airflow and specimen configuration.

tests.purpose: Test 35% O2 at 12 psi total pressure, with 4.2 psi O2 partial pressure, using planned test 3 as the nearby stepping stone and [saffire-v-4], [saffire-v-2] and [saffire-v-3] in [saffire-iv-vi] as the existing comparison evidence. This would extend oxygen coverage at fixed planned pressure and bring 8 untested grid squares within reach; no similar-pressure hardware precedent is supplied for this point.
tests.measure: Record ignition yes/no, flame spread rate where applicable, and extinction or sustained burning, retaining comparable specimen and airflow conditions for comparison with test 3.

tests.purpose: Test 38% O2 at 7 psi total pressure, with 2.66 psi O2 partial pressure, stepping from planned test 1 and extending comparisons with [saffire-vi-2], [saffire-vi-3] and [saffire-vi-4] in [saffire-iv-vi] to bring 8 untested grid squares within reach. This would establish evidence at the higher-oxygen, lower-pressure point; [cfi-1236] in [cfi] provides only similar-pressure precedent at 7.35 psi.
tests.measure: Record ignition yes/no, flame spread rate where applicable, and extinction or sustained burning, with actual atmosphere, airflow and specimen configuration.

openQuestions: Which solid fuels, specimen geometries and airflow conditions will be held comparable? The plan does not specify them, and CFI airflow is missing.
Which platform will provide partial gravity for the lunar test, or what is the stated justification for microgravity?
Can the selected hardware support each specified atmosphere? Similar recorded pressure does not establish oxygen capability; Saffire hardware details are absent.
Can the unknown outcomes for [saffire-v-4] and [saffire-v-3] be resolved? No nearby burned-and-went-out bracket is supplied for any test.
limitations: Coverage gains are conditional on completing the tests. The projected grid changes from 6 to 11 Tested cells and from 109 to 73 Untested cells; these are atmosphere-distance classifications, not predictions of ignition or flame spread.
The cited Saffire burned outcomes have a source-field basis in hand-transcribed published results [saffire-iv-vi]. Unknown outcomes do not establish extinction.
Every run in the supplied data is microgravity. Atmosphere proximity alone does not establish lunar applicability, and the available specimens do not represent all solid fuels.
The campaign supports engineering judgment; it does not replace NASA-STD-6001 or certified material testing.
